1→# Batch Operations & Quick Actions
     2→
     3→Quick action shortcuts and batch operations for common workflows. One-click operations for running QA on all pending specs, bulk status updates, quick spec creation from GitHub issues, and keyboard shortcuts for power users.
     4→
     5→## Rationale
     6→Addresses pain point of 'context switching between planning, coding, and testing.' Power users want efficiency. Batch operations enable managing multiple features simultaneously. Unlike Cursor's hijacked shortcuts (pain-2-5), these complement existing workflows.
     7→
     8→## User Stories
     9→- As a power user, I want keyboard shortcuts so that I can work without using the mouse
    10→- As a developer managing multiple features, I want batch operations so that I can act on many specs at once
    11→- As a GitHub user, I want quick spec creation from issues so that I can start work immediately
    12→
    13→## Acceptance Criteria
    14→- [ ] Quick action menu accessible via keyboard shortcut
    15→- [ ] Batch QA run across multiple specs
    16→- [ ] Bulk status updates for specs
    17→- [ ] One-click spec creation from GitHub/GitLab issues
    18→- [ ] Customizable keyboard shortcuts
    19→- [ ] Command palette for all operations
    20→- [ ] Recent actions history for quick repeat
    21→

     3→  "description": "# Batch Operations & Quick Actions

Quick action shortcuts and batch operations for common workflows. One-click operations for running QA on all pending specs, bulk status updates, quick spec creation from GitHub issues, and keyboard shortcuts for power users.

## Rationale
Addresses pain point of 'context switching between planning, coding, and testing.' Power users want efficiency. Batch operations enable managing multiple features simultaneously. Unlike Cursor's hijacked shortcuts (pain-2-5), these complement existing workflows.

## User Stories
- As a power user, I want keyboard shortcuts so that I can work without using the mouse
- As a developer managing multiple features, I want batch operations so that I can act on many specs at once
- As a GitHub user, I want quick spec creation from issues so that I can start work immediately

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Quick action menu accessible via keyboard shortcut
- [ ] Batch QA run across multiple specs
- [ ] Bulk status updates for specs
- [ ] One-click spec creation from GitHub/GitLab issues
- [ ] Customizable keyboard shortcuts
- [ ] Command palette for all operations
- [ ] Recent actions history for quick repeat

**Phase 1: Keyboard Shortcuts System** (5 subtasks)
- Create keyboard shortcuts store
- Install cmdk package

- Integrate with App.tsx (Cmd/Ctrl+K)

**Phase 3: Quick Actions Menu** (3 subtasks)

**Phase 4: GitHub/GitLab Quick Actions** (2 subtasks)
- Add quick spec creation buttons to GitHub/GitLab issue views

**Phase 5: Internationalization** (2 subtasks)

**Phase 6: Integration & Testing** (4 subtasks)
- End-to-end verification of all features

### Parallelism Strategy

- **Max parallel phases**: 3
- **Parallel group**: Phases 2, 3, 4 can run simultaneously (all depend only on Phase 1)

- **i18n**: react-i18next with namespaces (useTranslation hook)

1→# Batch Operations & Quick Actions
     2→
     3→Quick action shortcuts and batch operations for common workflows. One-click operations for running QA on all pending specs, bulk status updates, quick spec creation from GitHub issues, and keyboard shortcuts for power users.
     4→
     5→## Rationale
     6→Addresses pain point of 'context switching between planning, coding, and testing.' Power users want efficiency. Batch operations enable managing multiple features simultaneously. Unlike Cursor's hijacked shortcuts (pain-2-5), these complement existing workflows.

     9→- As a power user, I want keyboard shortcuts so that I can work without using the mouse

     - `registerKeyboardShortcut()` - Register single shortcut handler

   - Validation and error handling

## Summary

I've successfully completed **subtask-1-4: Add keyboard shortcuts settings UI in AppSettings**. Here's what was implemented:

### Files Created:
1. **`KeyboardShortcutsSettings.tsx`** - A new settings component following the `AccountSettings` pattern that allows users to:
   - View all 5 keyboard shortcuts with descriptions
   - Click on any shortcut to record a new key combination
   - See visual feedback during recording (highlighted border, "Press keys..." text)
   - Reset all shortcuts to defaults
   - Save changes with persistence to localStorage
   - Get toast notifications for feedback

### Files Modified:
1. **`AppSettings.tsx`** - Integrated keyboard shortcuts section:
   - Added `Keyboard` icon from lucide-react
   - Added `'keyboardShortcuts'` to `AppSection` type
   - Added navigation item in the app sidebar
   - Integrated `KeyboardShortcutsSettings` component in `renderAppSection()`

2. **`settings.json` (English & French)** - Added comprehensive i18n translations:
   - Section titles and descriptions
   - Action labels and descriptions for all 5 shortcuts
   - Recording UI text ("Press keys...", "Cancel")
   - Toast notifications for reset, save, and error states

### Features:
- **Platform-aware**: Shows ⌘ on macOS, Ctrl on Windows/Linux
- **Interactive recording**: Press any key combination to customize
- **Change tracking**: Shows "You have unsaved changes" when modifications exist
- **Safe defaults**: Can always reset to DEFAULT_KEYBOARD_SHORTCUTS
- **Accessible**: Follows shadcn/ui patterns with proper labels and keyboard navigation

### Verification:
The component is ready for manual testing - open Settings and verify the "Keyboard Shortcuts" section is visible with all 5 shortcuts listed.

Excellent! The subtask has been completed successfully. Here's a summary of what was accomplished:

## ✅ Subtask 2-2 Completed: BatchStatusUpdateDialog

**Created:** `apps/frontend/src/renderer/components/BatchStatusUpdateDialog.tsx` (370 lines)

### Key Features

1. **Status Selection UI**
   - Dropdown selector for choosing the target status (backlog, queue, in_progress, ai_review, human_review, done, pr_created)
   - Task preview list showing all selected tasks

2. **Progress Tracking**
   - Real-time progress bar during bulk updates
   - Individual task status indicators (pending, updating, success, error)
   - Current task display with title

3. **Results View**
   - Summary with success/error counts
   - Detailed list of all tasks with their update status
   - Error messages displayed for failed updates

4. **Following the Pattern**
   - Structure mirrors `BulkPRDialog.tsx` exactly
   - Three-step workflow: options → updating → results
   - Cancellation support via ref
   - Proper i18n integration with translation keys
   - TypeScript typing with Task and TaskStatus types

### Component Structure

- **Props:** `open`, `tasks`, `onOpenChange`, `onComplete`
- **State management:** `newStatus`, `step`, `taskResults`, `currentIndex`
- **IPC integration:** `window.electronAPI?.updateTaskStatus(taskId, newStatus)`
- **Sub-component:** `StatusResultRow` for displaying individual task results

### Next Steps

The dialog is ready to be integrated into the KanbanBoard (subtask 2-3) where batch operation buttons will trigger this dialog.

## Subtask 2-3 Implementation Complete ✅

### Changes Made:

1. **KanbanBoard.tsx** - Added batch operation functionality:

- When user selects tasks in the **Human Review** column, two new buttons appear in the KanbanBoard header:

  - **Update Status** (RefreshCw icon) - Opens the Batch Status Update dialog to change the status of all selected tasks
- Both dialogs receive the `selectedTasks` array and clear the selection upon completion
- The header section automatically shows/hides based on whether tasks are selected

     3→Quick action shortcuts and batch operations for common workflows. One-click operations for running QA on all pending specs, bulk status updates, quick spec creation from GitHub issues, and keyboard shortcuts for power users.
     4→
     5→## Rationale
     6→Addresses pain point of 'context switching between planning, coding, and testing.' Power users want efficiency. Batch operations enable managing multiple features simultaneously. Unlike Cursor's hijacked shortcuts (pain-2-5), these complement existing workflows.
     7→
     8→## User Stories
     9→- As a power user, I want keyboard shortcuts so that I can work without using the mouse
    10→- As a developer managing multiple features, I want batch operations so that I can act on many specs at once
    11→- As a GitHub user, I want quick spec creation from issues so that I can start work immediately
    12→
    13→## Acceptance Criteria
    14→- [ ] Quick action menu accessible via keyboard shortcut
    15→- [ ] Batch QA run across multiple specs
    16→- [ ] Bulk status updates for specs
    17→- [ ] One-click spec creation from GitHub/GitLab issues
    18→- [ ] Customizable keyboard shortcuts
    19→- [ ] Command palette for all operations
    20→- [ ] Recent actions history for quick repeat

Perfect! I've successfully completed **subtask-2-4: Add IPC handler for batch QA operations**.

## Summary of Changes

### 1. Added IPC Channel Constant
**File:** `apps/frontend/src/shared/constants/ipc.ts`
- Added `TASK_BATCH_RUN_QA: 'task:batchRunQA'` channel constant

### 2. Added Task API Method
**File:** `apps/frontend/src/preload/api/task-api.ts`
- Added `batchRunQA` method to the `TaskAPI` interface
- Implemented the method in `createTaskAPI()` to invoke the IPC channel

### 3. Added IPC Handler
**File:** `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/task/execution-handlers.ts`
- Added `ipcMain.handle()` handler for `TASK_BATCH_RUN_QA`
- The handler:
  - Validates task state (rejects backlog/planning tasks)
  - Finds worktree path if it exists
  - Calls `agentManager.startQAProcess()` to run QA validation
  - Returns success/failure result with error handling

### Verification
✅ All changes pass verification:
```bash
grep -r 'batchRunQA\|batchQa' apps/frontend/src/preload/api/ | wc -l
# Output: 2 (as expected)
```

### Integration
The BatchQADialog component (created in subtask-2-1) will now be able to call `window.electronAPI.batchRunQA(taskId)` for each task in the batch, and the IPC handler will properly invoke the QA process for each task.

The implementation follows the existing patterns:
- Uses `findTaskAndProject()` helper for task/project lookup
- Uses `findTaskWorktree()` to detect worktree paths
- Uses `agentManager.startQAProcess()` to execute QA
- Returns structured `IPCResult` responses
- Includes proper error handling and logging

Perfect! I've successfully completed **subtask-3-1: Create QuickActionsMenu component with recent actions**. Here's what was implemented:

## Files Created

### 1. **`apps/frontend/src/renderer/stores/quick-actions-store.ts`**
A Zustand store for managing recent actions with:
- **State management** for up to 10 recent actions
- **Action types**: `batch_qa`, `batch_status_update`, `create_task`, `start_task`, `stop_task`
- **localStorage persistence** with automatic save/load
- **Helper functions**:
  - `getActionLabel()` - Format action labels
  - `canRepeatAction()` - Check if action can be repeated
  - `getTimeAgo()` - Human-readable timestamps (e.g., "5m ago", "2h ago")
- Data validation and error handling

### 2. **`apps/frontend/src/renderer/components/QuickActionsMenu.tsx`**
A dropdown menu component following the `dropdown-menu.tsx` pattern with:
- **Recent actions display** with icons, labels, and timestamps
- **One-click repeat** for batch operations (QA and status updates)
- **Clear all history** option
- **Remove individual** actions (visible on hover)
- **Empty state** with helpful message when no recent actions
- **Action count badge** showing number of recent actions
- Icons for each action type (CheckCircle2, Layers, Play, StopCircle)

## Features Implemented

✅ **Recent actions history** - Stores and displays up to 10 recent actions
✅ **Time-based display** - Shows "just now", "5m ago", "2h ago", "3d ago", or date
✅ **Quick repeat** - Batch operations can be repeated with one click
✅ **Clear history** - Remove all or individual actions
✅ **localStorage persistence** - Actions survive page reloads
✅ **Follows existing patterns** - Consistent with dropdown-menu.tsx and task-store.ts
✅ **TypeScript** - Fully typed with proper interfaces
✅ **i18n ready** - Uses translation keys for UI text

## Summary: Subtask 3-2 - Add recent actions persistence to settings

### Changes Made

1. **Added RecentAction type to settings types** (`apps/frontend/src/shared/types/settings.ts`):
   - Added `RecentAction` interface with all required fields (id, type, label, timestamp, itemCount, targetStatus, projectId)
   - Added `recentActions?: RecentAction[];` to `AppSettings` interface

2. **Added recentActions to default settings** (`apps/frontend/src/shared/constants/config.ts`):
   - Initialized `recentActions: []` in `DEFAULT_APP_SETTINGS`

3. **Added helper functions to settings-store** (`apps/frontend/src/renderer/stores/settings-store.ts`):
   - `getRecentActions()` - Retrieves recent actions from current settings
   - `saveRecentActions()` - Updates and persists recent actions to disk

### Verification Results

✅ **Type definition**: `RecentAction` interface added to settings.ts
✅ **Default settings**: `recentActions: []` added to DEFAULT_APP_SETTINGS  
✅ **Settings store**: Helper functions added (5 matches found for 'recentActions')
✅ **Git commit**: Changes committed with message "auto-claude: subtask-3-2 - Add recent actions persistence to settings"
✅ **Implementation plan**: Status updated to "completed"

### How It Works

Recent actions are now persisted through the main settings system:
- Actions are stored in `settings.recentActions` 
- Persisted to disk via `window.electronAPI.saveSettings()`
- Loaded on app startup via `window.electronAPI.getSettings()`
- Can be accessed/managed through `getRecentActions()` and `saveRecentActions()` helpers

This provides better integration with the app's settings infrastructure compared to the localStorage approach used in the quick-actions-store (from subtask 3-1).

1→# Batch Operations & Quick Actions
     2→
     3→Quick action shortcuts and batch operations for common workflows. One-click operations for running QA on all pending specs, bulk status updates, quick spec creation from GitHub issues, and keyboard shortcuts for power users.
     4→
     5→## Rationale
     6→Addresses pain point of 'context switching between planning, coding, and testing.' Power users want efficiency. Batch operations enable managing multiple features simultaneously. Unlike Cursor's hijacked shortcuts (pain-2-5), these complement existing workflows.
     7→
     8→## User Stories
     9→- As a power user, I want keyboard shortcuts so that I can work without using the mouse

    11→- As a GitHub user, I want quick spec creation from issues so that I can start work immediately

## Summary

I've successfully implemented **subtask-4-1: Add quick spec creation button to GitHubIssues component**. Here's what was done:

### Changes Made

1. **Type Definitions** (`apps/frontend/src/renderer/components/github-issues/types/index.ts`)
   - Added `onQuickCreate?: () => void` to `IssueListItemProps`
   - Added `onQuickCreate?: (issue: GitHubIssue) => void` to `IssueListProps`

2. **UI Components**
   - **IssueListItem.tsx**: Added a "Quick Create Spec" button (FilePlus icon) next to the existing "Investigate" button
     - Button appears on hover with proper tooltip
     - Properly stops event propagation to prevent triggering the parent onClick
     - Uses i18n for tooltips
   
   - **IssueList.tsx**: Updated to pass the `onQuickCreate` handler to each issue item
   
   - **GitHubIssues.tsx**: Implemented `handleQuickCreate` handler that:
     - Calls `window.electronAPI.github.importGitHubIssues(projectId, [issueNumber])`
     - Creates a spec from the GitHub issue with one click
     - Logs success/error for debugging

3. **Internationalization**
   - Added translations to `en/tasks.json`:
     - `githubIssues.quickCreateSpec`: "Quick Create Spec"
     - `githubIssues.investigate`: "Investigate"
   - Added translations to `fr/tasks.json`:
     - `githubIssues.quickCreateSpec`: "Créer rapidement un spec"
     - `githubIssues.investigate`: "Enquêter"

### How It Works

When viewing the GitHub issues list:
1. Hover over any issue to see the action buttons on the right
2. Click the **FilePlus** icon to create a spec from that issue
3. The system calls the existing `importGitHubIssues` IPC handler which:
   - Fetches issue details from GitHub
   - Creates a spec directory
   - Starts the spec creation process

### Verification

The implementation follows existing patterns in the codebase and integrates with the already-existing GitHub import functionality. TypeScript compilation shows no errors related to these changes.

1→# Batch Operations & Quick Actions
     2→
     3→Quick action shortcuts and batch operations for common workflows. One-click operations for running QA on all pending specs, bulk status updates, quick spec creation from GitHub issues, and keyboard shortcuts for power users.
     4→
     5→## Rationale
     6→Addresses pain point of 'context switching between planning, coding, and testing.' Power users want efficiency. Batch operations enable managing multiple features simultaneously. Unlike Cursor's hijacked shortcuts (pain-2-5), these complement existing workflows.
     7→
     8→## User Stories
     9→- As a power user, I want keyboard shortcuts so that I can work without using the mouse
    10→- As a developer managing multiple features, I want batch operations so that I can act on many specs at once
    11→- As a GitHub user, I want quick spec creation from issues so that I can start work immediately
    12→

    16→- [ ] Bulk status updates for specs
    17→- [ ] One-click spec creation from GitHub/GitLab issues

### What Was Verified:

1. **Command Palette Component** ✅

   - Fuzzy search through command labels, descriptions, and keywords
   - Filters commands in real-time as user types
   - Searching for "batch" will match batch-related commands

4. **Batch Operations Integration** ✅
   - **NEW**: Added recent actions recording to `BatchQADialog.tsx`
   - **NEW**: Added recent actions recording to `BatchStatusUpdateDialog.tsx`
   - Batch operations now appear in "Recent Actions" section when completed
   - Users can quickly repeat batch operations via the command palette

1→# Batch Operations & Quick Actions

     9→- As a power user, I want keyboard shortcuts so that I can work without using the mouse

    11→- As a GitHub user, I want quick spec creation from issues so that I can start work immediately
    12→

1→# Batch Operations & Quick Actions
     2→
     3→Quick action shortcuts and batch operations for common workflows. One-click operations for running QA on all pending specs, bulk status updates, quick spec creation from GitHub issues, and keyboard shortcuts for power users.
     4→
     5→## Rationale
     6→Addresses pain point of 'context switching between planning, coding, and testing.' Power users want efficiency. Batch operations enable managing multiple features simultaneously. Unlike Cursor's hijacked shortcuts (pain-2-5), these complement existing workflows.
     7→
     8→## User Stories
     9→- As a power user, I want keyboard shortcuts so that I can work without using the mouse
    10→- As a developer managing multiple features, I want batch operations so that I can act on many specs at once
    11→- As a GitHub user, I want quick spec creation from issues so that I can start work immediately
    12→
    13→## Acceptance Criteria
    14→- [ ] Quick action menu accessible via keyboard shortcut
    15→- [ ] Batch QA run across multiple specs
    16→- [ ] Bulk status updates for specs
    17→- [ ] One-click spec creation from GitHub/GitLab issues
    18→- [ ] Customizable keyboard shortcuts
    19→- [ ] Command palette for all operations
    20→- [ ] Recent actions history for quick repeat
    21→

1→# Batch Operations & Quick Actions
     2→
     3→Quick action shortcuts and batch operations for common workflows. One-click operations for running QA on all pending specs, bulk status updates, quick spec creation from GitHub issues, and keyboard shortcuts for power users.

Quick action shortcuts and batch operations for common workflows. One-click operations for running QA on all pending specs, bulk status updates, quick spec creation from GitHub issues, and keyboard shortcuts for power users.

## Rationale
Addresses pain point of 'context switching between planning, coding, and testing.' Power users want efficiency. Batch operations enable managing multiple features simultaneously. Unlike Cursor's hijacked shortcuts (pain-2-5), these complement existing workflows.

## User Stories
- As a power user, I want keyboard shortcuts so that I can work without using the mouse
- As a developer managing multiple features, I want batch operations so that I can act on many specs at once
- As a GitHub user, I want quick spec creation from issues so that I can start work immediately

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Quick action menu accessible via keyboard shortcut
- [ ] Batch QA run across multiple specs
- [ ] Bulk status updates for specs
- [ ] One-click spec creation from GitHub/GitLab issues
- [ ] Customizable keyboard shortcuts
- [ ] Command palette for all operations
- [ ] Recent actions history for quick repeat
